Petitio vs. 1.The Food Safety Officer, Melpuram, Kanyakumari District. 2.The Adjudicating Authority, The District Revenue Officer, Kanyakumari District. ... Respond Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of I issuance of a Writ of Certiorari, to call for the records relating to impugned order passed by the second respondent Na.Ka.No.U1/20377/2018 dated 12.11..2018. For Petitioner : Mr.R.Parthiban For Respondents : Mr.Aayiram K.Selvakumar, Additional Government Pleader. 1/20 http://www.judis.nic.in R.Chandramohan vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194722421/ 1 W.P(MD)No.1288 Order
texts.facts: 2.A counter-affidavit dated 06.02.2019 has been filed by first respondent and in paragraph 1, first respondent has averred that the counter-affidavit is being filed on behalf of second respondent also. Therefore, both respondents have filed counter-affidavit and pleadings are complete. 3.Main writ petition is now taken up, heard out and is being disposed of. 4.Writ petitioner is manufacturing gingelly oil and is marketing the same under the brand 'CM Gold Palmolein Oil' (hereinafter referred to as 'said oil' for brevity). http://www.judis.nic.in 5.The first respondent had taken samples of said oil on 23.08.2017 from a store in Melpuram and proceedings under 'The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006' (hereinafter referred to as 'said Act' for brevity) were commenced. These proceedings under said Act culminated in an order dated 12.11.2018 bearing Reference Na.Ka.No.1/20377/2018 made by the second respondent which has been called in question in the instant Writ Petition. This order made by the second respondent which has been called in question in the instant Writ Petition shall hereinafter be referred to as 'impugned order' for the sake of brevity, clarity and convenience. Though the impugned order does not mention the provision of law under which the same has been made, there is no disputation or disagreement before this Court that the impugned order has been passed by the second respondent under Section 68 of said Act. Vide impugned order, second respondent has imposed penalties of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) each on the seller and shop owner besides a penalty of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) on the manufacturer. The seller and shop owner are not before this Court, but the manufacturer on whom a penalty of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) has been imposed vide impugned order is before this Court. http://www.judis.nic.in 6.Before proceeding further with this matter , it is to be noted that there is an appeal provision under said Act for assailing the impugned order. (5) The procedure of appeal and powers of the Tribunal shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government.' http://www.judis.nic.in 7.There is no disputation or disagreement before this Court that on the date of filing the instant Writ Petition ie., 22.01.2019, the Appellate Tribunal had not been constituted. In other words, alternate remedy provided under Section 70 of said Act is in ineffective as of today. 8.Now, reverting to the challenge to the impugned order, learned counsel for writ petitioner assailed the impugned order on three grounds. In other words, challenge to the impugned order is three fold, the same can be summarised and set out as follows: http://www.judis.nic.in a) The sample was drawn on 23.08.2017 and it was sent to the Food Analyst on the same day by courier, but the Food Analyst ultimately sent the analysis report to the Designated Officer only on 14.12.2017. Under Section 42(2) of said Act, the report should have been so sent within fourteen days from the date on which the Food Analyst received the sample from the Food Safety Officer. Therefore, there is a violation of Section 42(2) of said Act which is a mandatory requirement. b) The complaint being predicated on the report of the Referral Lab dated 07.03.2018 only talks about samples being Substandard and it is nobody's case that it was Misbranded whereas impugned order proceeds on the basis that it is Misbranded. R.Chandramohan vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194722421/ 3 c) Section 49 of said Act provides for parameters for quantification of penalty, but the impugned order is silent about said quantification and there is nothing to show the basis on which, Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) has been imposed as penalty on the writ petitioner. http://www.judis.nic.in 9.In response to the aforesaid three fold attack , learned State counsel made submissions which are as follows: a) With regard to report not being sent to Designated Officer within fourteen days by the Food Analyst, drawing the attention of this Court to Rule 2.4.2 of the 'Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011' (hereinafter 'said Rules' for brevity) and paragraph No.6 therein of Rule 2.4.2 of said Rules, it was submitted that fourteen days is not non-negotiable and there is a provision for delayed submission of the report. b) With regard to penalty being imposed on the ground of Misbranding (while complaint is 'Substandard') adverting to the impugned order, it is submitted by the learned state counsel that the impugned order proceeds on the basis that said sample is Substandard, whereas in the concluding paragraph portion alone word 'Misbranded' has been typed which is clearly a typographical error. It is learned State counsel's submission that writ petitioner is trying to make a mountain out of a mole hill.
texts.arguments: The appeal provision is Section 70 of said Act which reads as follows: '70. Establishment of Food Safety Appellate Tribunal. The Central Government or as the case may be, the State Government may, by notification, establish one or more tribunals to be known as the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions of the Adjudicating Officer under section 68. R.Chandramohan vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194722421/ 2 (2) The Central Government or the State Government, as the case may be, shall prescribe, the matters and areas in relation to which the Tribunal may exercise jurisdiction. (3) The Tribunal shall consist of one person only (hereinafter referred to as the Presiding Officer of the Tribunal) to be appointed, by notification, by the Central Government or the State Government, as the case may be: Provided that no person shall be qualified for appointment as a Presiding Officer to the Tribunal unless he is or has been a District Judge. (4) The qualifications, appointment, term of office, salary and allowances, resignation and removal of the Presiding Officer shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government. Section 49 of said Act reads as follows: 49. General provisions relating to penalty. While adjudging the quantum of penalty under this Chapter, the Adjudicating Officer or the Tribunal, as the case may be, shall have due regard to the following: (a) the amount of gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the contravention, (b) the amount of loss caused or likely to cause to any person as a result of the contravention, http://www.judis.nic.in R.Chandramohan vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194722421/ 4 (c) the repetitive nature of the contravention, (d) whether the contravention is without his knowledge, and (e) any other relevant factor.' 12.Paragraph No.3 of the impugned order reads as follows: '3) vjpjp 3 jug;g[ tHf;ffwpqh;: jdJ fl;rpf;fhuuhy; jahhpf;fg;gl;l mBj Oil tpUJefhpy; khjphp vLj;jjpy; Substandard vd bjhptpf;ftpy;iy. epakd mYtyh; gjpy; : tpUJefhpy; vLj;j khjphp Substandard ny;iy vd bjhptpj;jJ rl;g{h;tkhdJ my;y. btt;BtW jpdA;fspy; jahhhpj;J btt;BtW Lot Number-y; ghf;bfl; Bghlg;gLtjhy; nt;tHf;fpy; Substandard vd bjhptpf;fg;gl;l Palmolein Oil cld; xg;gpl KoahJ. czt[ ghJfhg;g[ mYtyh; mwpf;if vjphp 1, 2 MfpBahh; tpsf;fk; kw;Wk; vjphp 3 jug;g[ tpthjk;, gFg;gha;t[ Tl gFg;gha;t[ mwpf;if Mfpait ftdkhf ghprPypf;fg;gl;;lJ. jq;rht{h; czt[ gFg;gha;t[ Tl mwpf;ifapd;go 'The above said sample is Substandard under Section 3(1)z(x) of FSS Act 2006. This Court deems it appropriate to extract 42(2) of said Act and the same reads as follows: '42. Procedure for launching prosecution. (2) The Food Analyst after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer shall analyse the sample and send the analysis report mentioning method of sampling and analysis within fourteen days to Designated Officer with a copy to http://www.judis.nic.in Commissioner of Food Safety.' R.Chandramohan vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194722421/ 6 18.The rival submissions extracted supra would reveal that Rule 2.4.2 of said Rules and paragraph 6 are relevant, therefore they are extracted / reproduced and the same read as follows: '2.4.2. Analysis of food samples by Food Analyst 1.On receipt of the package containing a sample of food for analysis, the Food Analyst or an officer authorized by him shall compare the seals on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression of seal received separately and shall note the condition of the seal thereon. 2.Food laboratories including a mobile food laboratories wherever required, may be established or notified by the Central / State Government for the purpose of testing food samples received from the Food Safety Officer / purchaser. 3.If the sample container received by the Food Analyst is found to be in broken condition or unfit for analysis, he shall, within a period of seven days from the date of receipt of such sample, inform the Designated Officer about the same and request him to send the second part of the sample for analysis. 4.On receipt of requisition from the Food Analyst pursuant to Rule 2.4.2 93) the Designated Officer, shall by the succeeding working day, dispatch to the Food Analyst for analysis one part of the samples sent to him by the Food Safety Officer. 5.On receipt of the sample, the Food Analyst shall anaylse or cause to be analysed the sample and send the analysis report mentioning the method of analysis. The analysis report shall be as http://www.judis.nic.in per Form VII A and four copies of the same shall be sent to the Designated Officer under whose jurisdiction the Food Safety Officer functions or the purchaser of article of food. The analysis report shall be signed by the Food Analyst and such report shall be sent within fourteen days of the receipt of the sample by the Food Analyst. 19.Equally important is sub-paragraph (iii) of paragraph No.5 of the counter affidavit of the respondents which reads as follows: '5(iii). The petitioner stated that the second respondent failed to consider that the Food Analyst had not sent report http://www.judis.nic.in within 14 days as contemplated under Section 42. , learned counsel for writ petitioner, adverting to the statement of writ petitioner before the second respondent who made the impugned order, pointed out that a plea has been raised before the second respondent regarding violation of Section 42(2) of said Act qua time frame or in other words, plea that the Food Analyst has not sent the report to the Designated Officer within fourteen days from the date of receipt of sample has in fact been raised before the second respondent. This is articulated in the statement of writ petitioner before the second respondent and the relevant portion reads as follows: 'It is further submitted that the Food Analyst said to have given a report dated 20.12.2017 that the same was Misbranded and Substandard and did not comply with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
